name: Crowbone
description:
Crowbone is a percussion-forward genre born in GLMZ's maintenance corridors and transit junction warrens, where workers with industrial-grade skeletal reinforcements discovered that their augmented bones conducted vibration in musically interesting ways. Early Crowbone performers would strike their own chassis-reinforced limbs, ribs, and skulls with calibrated implements, broadcasting the internal resonance directly through bone-conduction neural taps. The genre rapidly evolved as performers began layering multiple skeletal performers in complex polyrhythmic arrangements, creating music experienced as much through proprioception as through conventional auditory channels.

Crowbone compositions are built around the principle of 'the body as the instrument it was always trying to be,' a phrase attributed to the genre's originating collective, the Marrow Engineers. Modern Crowbone has incorporated AI-assisted resonance mapping and subdermal transducers, but purists insist the genre's soul lives only in unaugmented bone-on-bone impact, arguing that software mediation destroys the essential suffering-as-music quality that defines the form.
creator: various
tier_availability: Tier 4-6; underground venues; limited neural feed distribution
legality: Legal; performances occasionally investigated under self-harm statutes
audience: Augmented laborers, body modification communities, industrial workers, underground music devotees
cultural_impact: Crowbone forced GLMZ's entertainment licensing bodies to develop entirely new regulatory categories around 'body-sourced performance,' a legal grey zone that remains contested. The genre has been adopted by several radical augmentation-rights groups as both anthem and argument — proof that the augmented body produces culture rather than merely consuming it. Upper-tier commentators frequently mischaracterize Crowbone as violent spectacle, a characterization its practitioners vigorously reject.
story_hooks: A Crowbone performer's skeletal augmentations were illegally manufactured and begin failing mid-tour, raising questions about who is responsible for the consequences
A Tier 1 music theorist attempts to formally analyze Crowbone and is radically changed by the immersive experience of attending her first live performance
The Marrow Engineers' original recordings are discovered to contain encrypted data hidden in the bone-resonance frequencies — someone used the music as a dead drop
